prompt: Swern oxidation (DMSO / (COCl)₂ / Et₃N, −78 °C) is a popular alternative to PCC for making aldehydes. What is its main practical advantage?

options.label: No toxic metal byproducts — all byproducts (dimethyl sulfide, CO, CO₂) are volatile and easily removed.
Much faster than PCC — reaction complete in minutes vs hours at room temperature.
Only Swern can oxidize ring alcohols to cyclic ketones; PCC fails on 5- and 6-membered rings.
Swern tolerates water in the reaction mixture, unlike PCC which decomposes in moist conditions.

explanation: Swern avoids chromium entirely — the activated DMSO oxidizes the alcohol, releasing DMS + CO + CO₂, all volatile. Big win for pharma (no Cr contamination). Downsides: must run at −78 °C and the DMS smell. Swern is strictly anhydrous (not water-tolerant), and PCC also works on cyclic alcohols fine.
